reasoning: His request resolves part of the prior abstention by implication: asking how to create titan-gate answers the prediction question, since a repo you are about to create has no files under evals/. I logged that as prediction entry one rather than letting it pass, per R6. The vocabulary blanks for receipt and the phase table remain unfilled, so cost_per_receipt and the unit_rule's phase claim stay blocked; the scoreboard's dependency order makes golden_set_size_owned the only reachable blank anyway, which is what this scaffold targets. I built and ran the whole thing here rather than handing him untested heredocs, because a pasted command sequence that has never executed is the same defect as an eval that has never seen a known-bad case. One correction to my own process: the smoke test labeled a hundred synthetic cases and sealed a holdout, which left the repo reporting golden_set_size_owned at its floor. Shipping that would have handed him a scoreboard that reads PASS on fabricated data. Stripped before packaging, and the clean-state gate re-run to prove it now reads BLOCKED.

gaming_vector: The golden set floor counts rows, not judgment. Labeling twenty-five obvious cases four times over, or letting one class dominate, reaches one hundred rows while producing a set on which any constant judge scores well. The scaffold makes the counter go up, which is the thing that feels like progress.
